card-art.joulz-navy.why: The default every new player wears: a flat navy panel with nothing on it.
card-art.joulz-navy.fix: A subtle navy-to-ink gradient with a faint bolt watermark and a soft top sheen, so even the default card feels finished.

card-art.bolt-stripes.why: Two thin diagonal stripes on navy; reads as unfinished at phone size.
card-art.bolt-stripes.fix: Bolder, glowing bolt stripes with depth (a darker under-stripe) and a light sweep.

card-art.grid.why: A faint 1 px grid that nearly disappears on a phone.
card-art.grid.fix: A perspective grid (horizon glow) rather than a flat one; doubles as a 'starter neon' look.

card-art.waves.why: Thin outline waves at low contrast; looks like a placeholder texture.
card-art.waves.fix: Layered filled waves with a gradient, like a night sea; keep the name area calm.

card-art.hexes.fix: Raised hex tiles with a soft bevel and a few lit cells.

card-art.circuit.why: Readable green traces with nodes; a decent free design.

card-art.dots.why: A dot grid at very low contrast; disappears on the strip.
card-art.dots.fix: A halftone fade (big dots to small) in a brand colour.

card-art.sunburst.why: Muddy brown rays; looks dated rather than premium.
card-art.sunburst.fix: Gold rays on deep navy with a glow at the centre, so it matches the brand gold.

card-art.tier.spark.why: Flat brown panel with one bolt; the lowest tier looks drab rather than bronze.
card-art.tier.spark.fix: A bronze metal finish (gradient, edge sheen) behind the bolt; the six tiers should step up in finish, not just hue.

card-art.tier.charge.why: Flat green panel with a single bolt; very close to its siblings.
card-art.tier.charge.fix: Give each tier its own finish step (bronze → silver → gold → platinum → obsidian → diamond) as the rarity ladder does.

card-art.tier.volt.fix: As Charge: a distinct finish per tier.

card-art.tier.lightning.why: Bright gold rays and bolts; reads as a top tier.

card-art.tier.top-500.why: The rarest card art is a washed-out beige; it looks less special than Lightning.
card-art.tier.top-500.fix: The most prestigious art in the game: diamond-plate or prism finish, animated sheen, a crown mark.

card-art.crimson.why: Rich red with chevrons; reads well at every size.

card-art.royal.why: The crown is a faint smudge behind the pill; at phone size it reads as a stain.
card-art.royal.fix: A crisp gold crown outline and filigree border; keep the navy.

card-art.emerald.why: Faceted green gem surface; looks like a paid item.

card-art.sunset.why: Clear synthwave sun and grid; strong at every size.

card-art.lava.why: A flat orange gradient with two faint arcs; Epic at 1,000 coins but looks like a free starter.
card-art.lava.fix: Molten cracks with an inner glow over dark rock, ember specks.

card-art.neon-city.why: Skyline with lit windows; good, the name stays readable.

card-art.gold-circuit.why: Gold traces on black; premium and on brand.

card-art.aurora.why: Legendary: animated aurora over mountains; clearly the best of the shop's card arts.

card-art.diamond-plate.why: Legendary, but the diamonds are clip-art stickers over a gold tread plate and crowd the right side.
card-art.diamond-plate.fix: Fewer, faceted diamonds set into the plate with real highlights; a slow light sweep across the plate.

card-art.frost.why: A snowflake is drawn through the player's name ('Sky*Racer') and the moon competes with it.
card-art.frost.fix: Move the flakes and moon to the right third, away from the name; keep the mountains.

card-art.neon-wave.why: Free-track Rare: dotted neon waves, fine for its level.

card-art.neon-skyline.why: Legendary (free level 60): the buildings and lit windows run behind the name and title, which then read poorly.
card-art.neon-skyline.fix: Keep the skyline to the right half or darken the left behind the name.

card-art.neon-pulse.why: Heartbeat line and rings; clean and on theme.

card-art.static.why: Premium level 14 Rare, but it is near-black noise you barely see on a phone.
card-art.static.fix: Visible TV static bands with a scan line and a little colour bleed.

card-art.grid-runner.why: Retro runner on a grid; good.

card-art.neon-circuit.why: Legendary: bold neon circuit and bolt; strong.

frame.plain.why: The default thin outline; correct for a default.

frame.bronze.why: A plain orange line (Common, free level 6); nothing says 'bronze'.
frame.bronze.fix: A metal bronze bevel with small corner studs.

frame.silver.why: A plain grey line (Rare, free level 26).
frame.silver.fix: A brushed-silver bevel with a light sweep at the corners.

frame.gold.why: Ornate gold with corner brackets; reads premium.

frame.obsidian.why: Elite at 1,600, but the triangle corners look like folded paper and the violet edge is faint.
frame.obsidian.fix: A glossy black frame with a crisp violet edge light and faceted corners.

frame.diamond.why: Legendary: prism edge with diamond corners; strong.

frame.founding.why: Earned; beautiful on the card, but on the 44 px nameplate strip the 'FOUNDER #0042' plaque is unreadable and the bolt tabs run into the score.
frame.founding.fix: A strip variant: no plaque text (or a small bolt mark) and nothing outside the strip's box.

frame.top-500.why: Earned, but its plaque shows the sample's fixed 'TOP 500 #214' (not the player's place), the crown is cut off at the top, and on the strip it covers the score.
frame.top-500.fix: Draw the player's own place (or no number), keep the crown inside the card's box, and a strip variant that stays inside the name area. Nothing grants it yet.

frame.neon-circuit.why: Elite (premium level 34): animated neon tubes; strong.

frame.championship.why: PLACEHOLDER: no art at all; equipping it draws the Plain frame.
frame.championship.fix: Draw it (animated, the most prestigious frame) before any Championship is held; until then don't grant it.

frame.s1-spark.why: PLACEHOLDER art (a generated metal outline with a 'SEASON 1' tab); the tab is unreadable on the strip.
frame.s1-spark.fix: Draw the seven Season 1 frames as a set, each with its tier's emblem; the tab hidden on the strip.

name-colour.gold-leaf.why: Metallic gold with a dark edge; premium.

name-colour.chrome.why: Epic at 1,000, but it reads as plain grey text at phone size.
name-colour.chrome.fix: A real chrome gradient (bright top, dark band, bright bottom) with a white glint.

name-colour.sapphire.why: Blue metal with a deep shadow; fine.

name-colour.neon-pink.why: Free level 10 Common: a flat pink fill, the same as a plain colour.
name-colour.neon-pink.fix: A neon tube look: a light core with a pink glow, as Emerald Glow does.

name-colour.neon-cyan.why: Premium level 3 Rare: a flat cyan fill.
name-colour.neon-cyan.fix: As Neon Pink: a glowing tube.

name-colour.neon-red.why: Premium level 18 Rare: a flat red fill; red names also read as 'error'.
name-colour.neon-red.fix: A glowing tube in a warmer red-orange.

name-colour.electric-orange.why: The pixel font (Silkscreen) becomes hard to read on the 44 px strip and long names lose letters.
name-colour.electric-orange.fix: Keep the orange glow in the normal font, or keep pixels only on the full card.

card-back.royal-damask.why: A handsome back, but today it shows only in Full House (practice only since 1 Nov), on one small card.
card-back.royal-damask.fix: Show backs in more games (section 5) before selling it; the art itself can stay.

card-back.holo-foil.why: Elite at 1,600: attractive, but seen only in Full House practice.

card-back.neon.why: Premium level 4: seen only in Full House practice.

game-skin.full-house.midnight-felt.why: Full House is retired from rooms (practice only); a 1,000-coin table for a practice-only game. Joe, 13 Nov: stops being sold; owned felts stay usable.
game-skin.full-house.midnight-felt.fix: Leaves the Card Table bundle (README section 6: Proposal A puts the Aurora card art in its place).

game-skin.full-house.crimson-velvet.why: As Midnight Felt (Joe, 13 Nov: stops being sold; owned felts stay usable).

game-skin.full-house.neon-felt.why: Premium pass level 12 for a practice-only game.
game-skin.full-house.neon-felt.fix: Replace the pass level with a Five Hands or Summit look, or coins.

game-skin.crazy-golf.watermelon.why: The ball is about 8 px across on a phone; the skin is barely visible during play.
game-skin.crazy-golf.watermelon.fix: Show it where it can be seen: a larger ball draw is not allowed (nothing bigger), so add a short trail and a bigger skinned ball on the hole-in and the reveal.

game-skin.crazy-golf.disco.why: As Watermelon: invisible at play size.

game-skin.crazy-golf.neon-glow.why: Free level 14: as Watermelon, though its glow helps a little.

game-skin.crazy-golf.plasma.why: As Watermelon; the approved plasma glow is fainter than the art.
game-skin.crazy-golf.plasma.fix: Match the approved glow (section 4) and add the trail.

game-skin.cue-ball.pixel-pool.why: At play size the balls are ~16 px; the approved pixel digits read as smudges.
game-skin.cue-ball.pixel-pool.fix: Pixel digits drawn on whole device pixels (3 × 5) as the art shows; a pixel cue.

game-skin.cue-ball.galaxy-set.why: Elite at 1,600: at play size the nebula balls read as dark dots and the numbers vanish.
game-skin.cue-ball.galaxy-set.fix: Lighter nebula with brighter stars and a clear number disc; it must stay as legible as the default set.

game-skin.cue-ball.neon-8-ball.why: Free level 36: changes one ball; hardly noticed.
game-skin.cue-ball.neon-8-ball.fix: Add the neon cue and a neon pocket flash when the 8 drops.

game-skin.cue-ball.neon-ball-set.why: Rims show, but the approved glow is missing.
game-skin.cue-ball.neon-ball-set.fix: The approved outer glow inside the ball's 2 px allowance (section 4).

game-skin.top-bins.comet.why: The ball sits large near the camera; the comet ball reads well.

game-skin.apex.racing-stripes.why: The car is large on screen; stripes read clearly.

game-skin.apex.molten-gold.why: Legendary: gold car with shine; clearly premium.

game-skin.curl-champ.glacier.why: Only the player's own stone changes, and at the far end it is a few pixels; the handle the art shows is a flat bar.
game-skin.curl-champ.glacier.fix: The approved handle shape (section 4) and a frosty trail while sliding.

game-skin.curl-champ.aurora.why: As Glacier; the aurora swirl on the stone top is lost at play size.
game-skin.curl-champ.aurora.fix: As Glacier, with a stronger aurora band.

game-skin.curl-champ.neon-stones.fix: As Glacier, with the approved neon handle.

world-theme.apex.neon-night.why: Legendary: the night circuit looks good, but the approved chasing kerbs and pulsing lights are slower and dimmer than the art.

world-theme.crazy-golf.neon-course.why: Legendary (free level 50): strong, but the windmill's neon sails are flat compared with the art.

world-theme.curl-champ.neon-rink.why: Elite: dark ice with pink lines; plain next to the other three themes.
world-theme.curl-champ.neon-rink.fix: Ice with a faint reflected neon city, glowing house rings that pulse once when a stone stops.

world-theme.cue-ball.neon-table.why: Elite: a convincing neon table; strong.

avatar-finish.chrome.why: On the card the avatar is ~70 px and the finish changes a small helmet disc; Chrome, Pearl gem and Diamond gem look almost the same.
avatar-finish.chrome.fix: A finish should change the whole avatar (body and scene) with a visible material: reflections for Chrome.

avatar-finish.carbon.why: Reads as 'dark avatar'; the weave is invisible at card size.
avatar-finish.carbon.fix: A larger, higher-contrast weave and a red accent line.

avatar-finish.comic-ink.why: Bold outline and halftone read even small; distinctive.

avatar-finish.holographic.why: Elite: a pastel tint, easily mistaken for a gem colour.
avatar-finish.holographic.fix: A moving rainbow foil (still under Reduce Motion) across the whole avatar.

avatar-finish.wireframe.why: Elite: cyan wireframe reads clearly and looks special.

avatar-finish.lightning-core.why: Legendary: ring and sparks; clearly the top finish.

avatar-finish.neon-glow.why: Premium level 40: a pink glow round a small disc.
avatar-finish.neon-glow.fix: A glow round the whole avatar silhouette, plus a neon rim.

avatar-accessory.neon-bolt.why: Premium level 52: a tiny bolt over the head; at card size it is a few pixels.
avatar-accessory.neon-bolt.fix: Larger (within the avatar box), glowing, and drawn on every avatar shape the same way.

avatar-special-edition.neon-captain-joul.why: Premium level 1 (the pass's headline): pink neon helmet; distinctive.

reaction.banter.why: Four clear stickers; readable at chat size.

reaction.retro-arcade.why: Epic at 1,000: four plain boxes with small pixel words ('GLHF' is hard to read).
reaction.retro-arcade.fix: Fuller pixel stickers (coin, 1UP, heart) with colour and a pixel shadow.

reaction.captains-calls.why: Epic at 1,000: plain white speech bubbles with ~7 px text; the cheapest-looking pack.
reaction.captains-calls.fix: Captain Joulz himself in each sticker (the approved ready and win poses) with a short line.

reaction.spark.why: Free level 22: a 'pack' of a single star.
reaction.spark.fix: Two to four emotes per pack, or call it a single emote.

reaction.neon-signs.why: 'BRB CRYING' is unreadable at 34 px; the signs' text is thin.
reaction.neon-signs.fix: Shorter words and thicker neon strokes so each reads at chat size.

celebration.spotlight.why: Epic at 1,000: two faint grey cones; most players won't notice it.
celebration.spotlight.fix: Warm stage spotlights with dust in the beams and a sweep onto the winner.

celebration.shockwave.why: Elite at 1,600: three thin rings; looks unfinished.
celebration.shockwave.fix: A visible energy ring with distortion and sparks, in the brand gold.

celebration.power-surge.why: Legendary: lightning and stage glow; strong.

celebration.circuit-overload.why: Elite (premium level 58, the podium entrance): two flat lines; weak for the pass's late levels.
celebration.circuit-overload.fix: Traces that light up along the podium with nodes flashing, ending in a burst.

tile-style.brushed-gold.why: Gold border; clearly a paid look.

tile-style.circuit-trace.why: Free level 16: almost identical to the plain tile.
tile-style.circuit-trace.fix: Visible traces across the tile's border.
